title: Build a website you own.
description: The live reference site for Provelopment Foundation: see how pages are written, how the site adapts, and how to make it your own.

sections.lede: Foundation is an open-source website template designed to be understandable, editable and deployable. You can use it yourself, modify it as needed and take it wherever you choose.

sections.heading: Two ways to write a page

items.title: Markdown
items.body: For straightforward pages, Markdown keeps the content close to plain text, with simple notation for headings, lists and links. The **About** page on this site is written this way.

items.title: JSON
items.body: For structured pages, JSON defines sections such as heroes, columns, cards, tables and questions using a documented set of options. **This page** is written this way.

sections.heading: You own your website
sections.body: Using Provelopment services is a choice, not a requirement. Your website, its content and its code remain yours.

items.title: A working Foundation site
items.body: This website is the live reference deployment of the Foundation template. It runs the public code and includes example pages using both supported authoring methods.

sections.heading: Built to adapt
sections.body: The **Layout** control in the header switches between the Sidebar and Menu-bar presentations without changing the page, its address or its content. Foundation can also support multiple languages, physical locations and countries. When those options are configured, their controls appear in the same area. This reference site uses one language and no locations, so only the Layout control is shown.

sections.heading: The complete site is public
sections.body: This page is part of the site itself, not a mock-up. Its content comes from a single file — `home.json` — in the Provelopment Foundation repository. The About page, styling and site settings are there as well. Change the files, commit them and push the changes, and the site can rebuild from the updated source. The code remains yours to use, change and deploy elsewhere.
